lines.derivation: %s copies musl; %d includes the minus sign on -42; %u is decimal 42; 0x2a = 2*16+10 gives lowercase 2a; %c writes Z. The format ends with LF.

Default alignment is right, padded with spaces: xy has length 2 in width 8 (6 spaces); -7 length 2 in width 6 (4); 9 length 1 in width 6 (5); ab length 2 in width 6 (4); Q length 1 in width 3 (2). Followed by LF.
%.3s copies the first 3 bytes abc. Integer precision counts digits, excluding the sign: -12 becomes -00012 for 5 digits; 23 becomes 00023; hexadecimal ab becomes 00ab for 4 digits. Followed by LF.

The selected x86_64 musl target has 32-bit int: INT_MIN=-2^31, INT_MAX=2^31-1, UINT_MAX=2^32-1, whose 8 hexadecimal digits are all f. Integer zero with precision 0 emits no digits inside the brackets. Followed by LF.

%s copies tail; signed -1, unsigned zero, hexadecimal 0x10 (16 decimal) and character ! are separated by colons. There is no LF and no explicit flush: normal return from main must flush this final buffered output.
